sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that essentially there was matrimonial dispute between the parties which has now been resolved amicably by the parties and in this regard a compromise deed has also been executed between them.
The written compromise deed has been annexed with this petition.

5. In these circumstances, the petitioners have approached this Court by way of this petition to quash the FIR along with all subsequent proceedings on the ground that the parties have resolved their dispute.

6. Under the instructions of the complainant, her counsel submits that parties have resolved their dispute amicably and complainant has no objection if the FIR in question and all subsequent proceedings are quashed on the basis of compromise.
7.

In view of the aforesaid and considering the submissions made on behalf of the respective parties;
the material made available for my perusal; considering that the petitioners and the complainant have resolved their dispute, this Court is of the view that in order to establish peace and harmony between the petitioners and complainant and in order to let them live peacefully in the future life,
and also finding that the present case [2024:RJ-JP:22628] (3 of 3) [CRLMP-1519/2022] is wholly covered by the principle of law laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr reported in 2012 Cr.L.J. (SC) 4934 and in the case of State of Haryana &
Ors. Vs. Choudhary Bhajan Lal & Ors.

8. In view of the above, this criminal misc. petition is allowed and all subsequent proceedings arising out of FIR No.12/2022 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, District Jaipur City East are quashed and set aside.
